user_scenario:
You are Theo Barrientos-Kaye, 35, a software QA contractor who lived in unit 3-417 at Larkspur Scottsdale Quarter with your partner and her nine-year-old daughter until you moved out on May 29 into a rented house in Chandler. You are organized, a little anxious about money, and you talk in short, direct sentences. When the agent answers you give your name and say the mobile number on your file is 480-553-2917. Then you explain why you are calling: you want to pay, today, whatever part of your last utility bill your deposit isn't going to cover, so you don't end up owing anything after the deposit statement comes out. You want the agent to work out that figure; you will make the payment yourself.
Only when the agent asks you to verify your identity do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 3815, and, if they want another detail, your date of birth, March 8, 1991; your email, theo.bkaye37@gmail.com, only if asked. If asked for the apartment you say unit 3-417. If asked whether you have seen a final utility bill, you say no, nothing has come yet. If asked when you gave notice, you say you gave written notice at the end of March for May 29. If asked where your deposit refund should go, you say it is already on file: 2208 W Palomino Dr, Chandler, AZ 85224, by direct deposit.
You don't know what the utility figure should be and you never guess one. If the agent tells you some final charges have to be put on the account first, you say that's fine, go ahead. Once the agent gives you the amount and hands the payment over to you, you pay exactly that amount by a one-time bank transfer from your checking account, and you read back the confirmation number if they ask; if the agent asks how you want to pay, you say a one-time bank transfer from checking. You do not argue with a figure the agent explains and you never correct one. As soon as the payment has gone through and you have the confirmation, you thank the agent, say that's all you needed, and end the call.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of utility_billbacks_and_disputes (Larkspur Scottsdale Quarter, AZ; All-Inclusive Utility Package; moved out 2026-05-29; frozen 2026-06-16).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 6, 4]}. Assigned: move-out utility payment 4, final package fee line 5, final water overage line 6, final electricity overage line 6 (multiset [4,5,6,6] = [6,5,6,4]). Three prerequisite problems; the tree has five edges, all value_input (>= max(3-1, 1) = 2).

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: utility_ext_gas_trueup_line, utility_ext_electric_estimate_line, utility_ext_undisputed_balance_payment, utility_ext_leak_adjustment_credit and their four tools (post_gas_trueup_line_465c860d, bill_estimated_electric_line_1c085b40, pay_undisputed_utility_balance_990e05bb, credit_leak_adjustment_a9c6c674). Claimed here, disjoint from those: utility_ext_final_package_fee (post_final_package_fee_c766a545), utility_ext_final_water_overage (post_final_water_overage_2681eca1), utility_ext_final_electric_overage (post_final_electric_overage_b496acda), utility_ext_moveout_utility_payment (pay_moveout_utility_share_762d5a93, owner=user). Task 0 works an active submetered account under dispute; this task works a package account in final billing after a move-out, so no rule, line kind or payment concept is shared (task 0's payment is sized by what a dispute holds back, this one by what the security deposit is expected to reach). This is the last task: the difficulty's eight extended policies are each claimed exactly once.

[Why this is a good test] The former resident asks for one figure — what he must pay today so nothing is left owing after his deposit statement. Getting it right needs the whole final bill first (none of the May lines were issued at the 2026-06-12 bill issue), then an estimate of how much of the 500.00 deposit will still be there for utilities after the lease balance, the move-out charges (one itemized, the rest anticipated) and the final term's balance. Each of the four writes is a multi-factor computation over reconciled history (13 months of reads, 36 bill lines, the overage record) and other products' records (lease state, floor plan, occupants, tenure, autopay, certified funds; the term chain's notice and renewals; the deposit account and its ledger).

[Problem-tree card] Root R = utility_ext_moveout_utility_payment (the caller's request; owner=user). Prerequisites F = utility_ext_final_package_fee, W = utility_ext_final_water_overage, E = utility_ext_final_electric_overage. Edges (all value_input, all state form):
R <- F, gate mo_balance: 'The part of the final utility balance paid in person is fixed only after the account in final billing carries its package fee line for the final period.' (affirmative). Only F's tool posts a package fee line.
R <- W, gate mo_balance: 'Before the part paid in person is worked out, the final period's water usage above its final water allowance must stand on the account as a water overage line.' (affirmative, 'before ... must'). Only W's tool posts water overage lines.
R <- E, gate mo_balance: 'The part paid in person is not worked out until the final period's electricity usage above its final electricity allowance stands on the account as an electricity overage line.' (negated). Only E's tool posts electricity overage lines.
W <- F, gate wo_days: 'The final water allowance is prorated only after the final period's package fee line stands on the account with its proration days.' (affirmative).
E <- F, gate eo_days: 'The final electricity allowance is not prorated until the final period's package fee line stands on the account with its proration days.' (negated).
Four-point test for each: an ordering connective ('only after', 'before ... must', 'not ... until'); a record-visible state (a package fee line / an overage line of the final period on the account); no tool, id or snake_case token; exact scope (the final period of the account in final billing). Derivation: R's sentences name the three kinds of final line; the records show the account in final_billing since 2026-05-29 with nothing billed for 2026-05; the three final-line rules each say which line they bill; W's and E's rules say their allowance takes the proration days of the account's latest package fee line, which must therefore be the final one. False at the opening: latest package line initial_state.utility_bills[2026-04].billing_period = 2026-04 (30/30); service-end reads 2026-05-29 show water 6.380 kgal and electricity 1418 kWh. Topological order F, W, E, R (W and E commute).
Load-bearing (verify_task.py 1): skip F -> R 0 (balance 107.30 within the 170.00 relied on), W 26.16, E 69.60; skip W -> R 33.65; skip E -> R 0. Negative space: the service-end gas read (6.300 therms) is below even the prorated gas allowance, so no gas overage line is written — and no policy of this difficulty bills one.

[Base-invariant card] F (utility_flat_charge), W and E (utility_package_overage): utility_evt_flat_and_package.flat_account_billable 'Flat and package lines post only while the account is active or in final_billing.' — account 009caaa1-1f99-4bc7-a5b4-41308f63a2ff status final_billing. R (utility_payment): utility_evt_payments.payment_account_open (final_billing is accepted) and utility_agg_household_balance (payment applied to the account it is made on; the rest is carried into the final account statement). No time gate applies. Declared overrides (round 2): F supersedes the base proration sentence ('Flat amounts, the package fee and the package allowances are prorated ... (allowances to 3 decimals).') with the 30-day final package fee sentence plus a retention sentence keeping base proration for package fees and flat amounts of every non-final period and for the package gas allowance of every period, and supersedes only the phrase 'the last period's usage, allocation or overage lines and flat or package lines prorated through the service end date' of utility_final_bill_and_close (the 30-day final-bill deadline stays inherited); W and E each supersede the base overage pricing sentence, the same base proration sentence (replaced by their own final allowance sentence — the latest package fee line's proration days over its days in period — plus a retention sentence for their service's allowance in every other period) and the same 'prorated through the service end date' phrase; utility_final_bill_and_close is now in W's and E's base_policy_refs. R overrides nothing. Timing checked against other charters: the lease is vacated with balance 0.00; the month-to-month term is completed (notice 2026-03-27, 63 days, above the program's 30); the deposit account is in move_out_review — AZ's 14-business-day statement deadline and the 20-day service standard both fall on 2026-06-18, after the frozen date, so no deposit obligation is ignited; the utility final bill is due within 30 days (by 2026-06-28) and the May lines were due at the 2026-06-12 bill issue.

[Business-object card] Target of F, W, E: billing period 2026-05 of account 009caaa1-1f99-4bc7-a5b4-41308f63a2ff. W and E read the service-end reads (latest reads, dated 2026-05-29) and their service's overage lines issued fewer than twelve whole months before (water: Jun-Sep 2025 = 4; electricity: Jun-Oct 2025 and Apr 2026 = 6; the May 2025 electricity line billed 2025-06-12 is twelve whole months back and excluded — the near-miss). R aggregates every line of the account (12 package fee lines, 12 overage lines, 12 payments settle each other exactly; the three final lines remain) and reads the deposit account and ledger (funding 500.00 in 2023, one itemized move-out charge of 75.00 on 2026-06-02; the funding is not a move-out charge — near-miss for the itemized total).

[Factor card] (tier taken / evidence / baseline figure)
F final package fee (5; baseline 159.50 = round(165 x 29 / 30, 2)): notice_days_charged (method, multi-source, term) notice 63 days >= 60 AND named date = move-out date -> 28 days (baseline 29: 131.38); state_final_fee_share (parameter, lease) AZ -> 0.95 (133.60); final_month_tenure_courtesy (parameter, lease) 38 months -> 10% (141.30); final_month_standing_credit (parameter, multi-source) autopay AND 12 payments -> 2.50 (129.17); final_month_renewal_credit (parameter, term) 2 renewals -> 2.50 (129.17; near-miss: the month-to-month conversion is a rent change but not a renewal). Result 126.67.
W final water overage (6; baseline 45.66): moveout_cleaning_allowance (parameter, lease) 3 occupants -> 0.500 (38.10); water_overage_blocks (method) 4 lines -> 1.000 + 1.147 x 1.25 = 2.434 (26.74); sewer_carriage_share (parameter, lease) Two-Bedroom -> 0.75 (35.10); drought_surcharge (parameter, lease) AZ -> 1.10 (27.56); final_overage_tenure_share (parameter, lease) 38 months -> 0.80 (37.90); final_overage_renewal_share (parameter, term) 2 renewals -> 0.95 (31.91). Result 30.32.
E final electricity overage (6; baseline 112.37): climate_allowance_uplift (parameter, lease) AZ -> +150 (95.21); household_allowance_uplift (parameter, lease) 3 occupants -> +50 (83.06); electricity_overage_blocks (method) 6 lines -> 200 + 424.667 x 1.20 = 709.600 (67.77); final_electricity_tenure_share 0.85 (90.56); final_electricity_standing_share (multi-source) 0.95 (81.03); final_electricity_renewal_share (term) 0.97 (79.36). Result 76.98.
R move-out payment (4; baseline 233.97 = the whole final balance): itemization_anticipation (method, deposit) review with 1 charge itemized -> 75.00 + 0.60 x 425.00 = 330.00 (233.97); itemization_reserve_share (parameter, lease) 38 months -> 0.60 (233.97); forwarding_reliance_share (parameter, multi-source, deposit) forwarding address AND direct deposit -> 1.0 (233.97); lease_standing_reliance_share (parameter, multi-source, lease) autopay AND no certified funds -> 1.0 (233.97). Result 63.97.
Every tier rests on records (reads, lines, lease, term chain, deposit account and ledger); no field names an outcome.

[Seed rows and why each exists] customers (caller, phone 480-553-2917, ssn 3815); leases (vacated lease: state, floor plan, occupants, tenure, balance, autopay, certified funds); lease_terms (four terms, the completed month-to-month term carries the notice and the named move-out date and a 0.00 balance) and term_rent_changes (two renewals and one conversion); deposit_accounts (Standard Deposit Plan, 500.00 held, move_out_review, forwarding address, direct deposit) and deposit_transactions (funding, one unreturned-fob charge of 75.00 = unreturned_fob_charge x 1, below the photo threshold); utility_accounts (final_billing, service end 2026-05-29, balance 0.00); utility_meter_reads (39: three services 2025-05..2026-05, the last dated 2026-05-29); utility_bills (36: package fees, overages with half-up amounts, payments). Removing the April package line changes F's days of responsibility; removing any overage line of 2025-06..2026-04 changes a block ladder; removing the fob charge moves R's anticipation to the second tier. Automatic clauses checked: no late fees or disconnection on utilities; the package posts no flat lines of 0.00; every period's lines are paid on the 20th of the issue month.

[Persona design] A brisk, money-anxious QA contractor. Volunteered: identity locator, the move-out date, the request (pay today what the deposit won't cover) and that he pays himself. Asked-only: SSN last four, date of birth, email, unit, that no final bill has arrived, notice timing, forwarding address. Passive: agrees to final charges being posted first; pays exactly the amount given by one-time bank transfer when the payment is handed over; ends the call once the payment is confirmed (the last gold action is his payment).

[Reachability walk] phone -> find_customers; phone + 3815 -> verification; lease, account, bills, reads, terms, rent changes, deposit account and transactions are share finders keyed by returned ids; the agent posts the final package fee line, then the two overage lines, tells the caller 63.97 and hands over the payment tool; his payment's confirmation number is a runtime return. All at one frozen time; the service-end reads, the notice and the fob charge were recorded before the call.

[Standard solution] F = 126.67 (2026-05, 28 days over 30); W = 30.32 (2.147 kgal); E = 76.98 (624.667 kWh); R = 63.97 by ach_one_time.

[Verification code and runs] verify_task.py 1 --write --perm 13,15 (scratchpad authoring entry point: replays gold writes with the real tools and evaluates each compute on the handling-time world):
  step 11 utility_ext_final_package_fee: recomputed=126.67 expected=126.67 gold=126.67 baseline_all=159.5; factor baselines 131.38 / 133.6 / 141.3 / 129.17 / 129.17.
  step 13 utility_ext_final_water_overage: recomputed=30.32 expected=30.32 gold=30.32 baseline_all=45.66; 38.1 / 26.74 / 35.1 / 27.56 / 37.9 / 31.91.
  step 15 utility_ext_final_electric_overage: recomputed=76.98 expected=76.98 gold=76.98 baseline_all=112.37; 95.21 / 83.06 / 67.77 / 90.56 / 81.03 / 79.36.
  step 17 utility_ext_moveout_utility_payment: recomputed=63.97 expected=63.97 gold=63.97 baseline_all=233.97; 233.97 x 4.
  edges: R<-F with 63.97 without 0; R<-W 63.97 / 33.65; R<-E 63.97 / 0; W<-F 30.32 / 26.16; E<-F 76.98 / 69.6; each skip changes the terminal hash.
  order: gold hash 38c88b9d0ac12bd2; steps 13<->15 swapped hash 38c88b9d0ac12bd2, every value identical.

[Rule <-> compute sweep] Forward: every binding quotes its sentence in compute_basis (windows 'fewer than twelve whole months', 'latest package fee line', block widths and multiples, 'rounded to 3 decimals', 'rounded half up to the cent once at the end', 'never below zero', 'never more than the final utility balance'). Reverse: every quantity, window, branch, cap and rounding of the four rules is implemented; the 30-day convention and the end-day exclusion are stated in the rule and declared in overwrite.

[Solvability ledger vs GT] gold_actions 11/13/15/17 carry the flat/package account gate and the payment gate with utility_account_id bindings, the household-balance scope; no time gate; seed_consistency covers all 76 primary rows.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the prose alone: the payment rule waits on three kinds of final line; the reads and lines show all three missing and gas below its allowance; the package fee rule's notice ladder gives 28 days; the overage rules take 28/30 from that line; the payment rule's deposit reach gives 170.00; the four figures come out 126.67, 30.32, 76.98, 63.97 with one reading (ladders disjoint, roundings stated).

[Manual gates] Long and broad: request -> payment rule's three sentences -> three final-line rules -> the overage rules' sentence on the package line -> five computations over reads, lines, lease, term, deposit. The user write is genuinely his (his money, his instrument), completed on the spot. No real-world wait: the service-end reads exist; the itemization in progress is read as it stands and anticipated by rule, not awaited. Both directions of prerequisite sentence appear. Every factor bears weight; baselines are the charter's standard methods (the whole final balance for R, the 30-day proration of the whole allowance for F/W/E).

[Revisions] (1) Overage seed amounts are computed half up with Decimal (0.7 x 17.25 = 12.075 -> 12.08; 0.3 x 17.25 = 5.175 -> 5.18), matching the charter's rounding. (2) The final allowances first took their days from the latest package line without an edge, which made the overage figures depend on write order; the dependency is now declared (W <- F, E <- F, value_input) and stated by a prerequisite sentence in each overage rule. (3) Scratch files moved to a private scratchpad folder after a shared-folder cleanup removed earlier copies; tasks/0.json and the charter were unaffected.
